samples.summary: Frontend duplicate CRDT parser: the new colSpan/rowSpan, cols and stylesJson bands are untested
samples.evidence: The diff adds four new bands to packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts: normalizeTableSpan on colSpan/rowSpan (~line 455), parseColumnWidthsAttr for the cols attribute (~475), and sanitizeDocStyles in getStyles() (~705). The new test block 'bands the numeric attributes a peer can write' (peerRead helper at line 3389) covers only fontSize, image size, cell padding, rowHeights and listLevel. Grep of packages/frontend/tests for stylesJson/getStyles returns no matches, and MAX_TABLE_SPAN/MAX_COLUMN_RATIO appear nowhere in packages/frontend. The pre-existing colSpan/rowSpan tests (lines 2719-2877) exercise applyCellSpan writes read back from the writing store's cache, not a peer parse of a poisoned attribute. This is the parser the live editor uses, the frontend has no tsc lane, and the diff's own rationale is that an unbanded Infinity rowSpan hangs every viewer's tab via expandCellRangeForMerges - a band wired to the wrong field here would ship undetected.
searchedFor: read new describe block in tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts

samples.summary: New slides band-numerics module has no test in its own package; the group-recursion and staticElements branches are covered nowhere
samples.evidence: A repo-wide grep for bandElementNumerics|bandLayoutNumerics|bandSlidesDocumentNumerics finds only source files, the two package entry points, the three frontend call sites and one docs design doc - no slides test file. Indirect coverage exists via the frontend tests, but it misses two branches: (a) the group branch (el.type === 'group' with MAX_GROUP_DEPTH) - the board test 'bands a group child' goes through YorkieBoardStore.readElement's own group recursion (yorkie-board-store.ts line 425-441), which builds children by calling readElement, never bandElementNumerics; and the snapshot-adapter tests use only a top-level text element. (b) bandLayoutNumerics' staticElements list is never exercised (the slides store test only poisons layouts[0].placeholders). A regression in either branch would leave poisoned bodies reaching computeLayout with no failing test.

samples.summary: The two pdf-painter normalizeListLevel call sites have no test
samples.evidence: The diff replaces `block.listLevel ?? 0` with `normalizeListLevel(block.listLevel)` at pdf-painter.ts lines ~367 and ~593, justified as 'a poisoned one from a peer would put NaN coordinates into pdf-lib'. Grep of packages/docs/test/export/pdf-painter.test.ts for listLevel/normalizeListLevel returns no matches, and the editor-tab-bullet paint test explicitly scopes itself to the editor's own paint pass ('One representative sink, on purpose... the PDF painter, the table renderer and the peer cursor... are left to the unit test of the band itself'). The unit test of normalizeListLevel cannot detect a call site reverted or wired to the wrong field, so an NaN-coordinate PDF export could ship green.

samples.summary: normalizeListLevel call sites in peer-cursor.ts and table-renderer.ts are untested
samples.evidence: Two more new call sites (peer-cursor.ts lines ~255 and ~395 for caret x, table-renderer.ts ~525 where the level is also a Map key) are added with the same NaN-geometry rationale. The change's own comment in editor-tab-bullet.test.ts states these are deliberately left to the band's unit test. A unit test of normalizeListLevel proves the function, not that these readers call it, so a caret that never paints inside a cell list would not fail any test.

samples.summary: Backend slides band: notes blocks, colSpan and the MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS count cap are not covered
samples.evidence: The new describe 'assertValidSlidesBody bands the numerics that reach docs layout' only builds decks whose first slide has a single text element with data.blocks, and only asserts rowSpan of the two spans. assertValidSlideBlocks is also applied to a slide's notes (per the controller doc comment), bandSlideCellNumerics bands colSpan as well as rowSpan, and bandSlideBlockNumerics slices columnWidths to MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS - none of those three is asserted in the spec. The docs package covers the equivalent logic in bandBlockNumerics, but the controller holds its own second copy of the walk, so a divergence there is invisible.
searchedFor: read the new describe in docs-content.controller.spec.ts

samples.summary: bandSlidesDocumentNumerics' layouts branch is untested on the snapshot path
samples.evidence: parseSlidesSnapshot/parseBoardSnapshot now run bandSlidesDocumentNumerics, which also walks root.layouts. The new tests in snapshot-adapters.test.ts ('bands a slides snapshot text body', 'bands a board snapshot text body', 'survives MemSlidesStore') only include slide elements and notes; no snapshot fixture carries a layout with a poisoned placeholder. The live-store equivalent is tested (yorkie-slides-store 'bands a layout placeholder spec a peer poisoned'), but the snapshot path constructs the document differently, so its layout branch is unexercised.

samples.summary: indent/outdent refactor: a mixed list-item + paragraph selection is not tested
samples.evidence: indent()/outdent() were restructured from one pass with an if/else into two passes (applyListLevelChanges, then a forEachBlockInSelection that skips list-items and moves marginLeft). The new tests cover either a pure list selection (list level carries nested children) or a caret on a lone paragraph ('toolbar indent still moves a plain paragraph by marginLeft'); the 'toolbar indent / outdent carry the subtree as well' case includes a paragraph but the caret is on b1, so the paragraph is never in the selection and only its undefined listLevel is asserted. A regression where the second pass double-indents or skips paragraphs inside a multi-block selection (or where marginLeft is applied to list items) would not fail.

samples.summary: FONT_SIZE_MAX = Math.min(400, MAX_FONT_SIZE) has no test asserting the invariant it documents
samples.evidence: The comment states the picker ceiling 'must stay at or under the model's', but no test asserts FONT_SIZE_MAX <= MAX_FONT_SIZE; the Math.min enforces it at runtime, so this is only a documentation-vs-test nit. Grep of packages/frontend for FONT_SIZE_MAX assertions against MAX_FONT_SIZE found none.

verdict.reason: The frontend duplicate parser bands colSpan/rowSpan (yorkie-doc-store.ts:460-461), cols (`:480`) and the named-style registry (`:700-714` via sanitizeDocStyles), but no frontend test exercises any of them with an out-of-band value. The new peer-read block (tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:3388-3499) covers only fontSize, image size, cell padding, rowHeights and listLevel. Repo-wide grep for normalizeTableSpan/parseColumnWidthsAttr/sanitizeDocStyles/MAX_TABLE_SPAN/MAX_COLUMN_RATIO hits only packages/docs (engine copy, which IS banded-tested at test/model/numeric-attrs.test.ts:283-320,403-441) and the backend; nothing under packages/frontend/tests or packages/frontend/src/**/__tests__. Every peer-read site in the frontend tests uses in-band values; the pre-existing span tests (2719-2945) go through applyCellSpan with valid spans, and the closest peer parse (yorkie-doc-store-concurrent.integration.ts:756-804,855-932) reads colSpan=2 and cols=[0.7,0.3] only, so it cannot fail if the band is missing or wired to the wrong field. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a changed behavior with no meaningful test; the untested failure mode (an unbanded Infinity rowSpan feeding expandCellRangeForMerges) hangs every viewer's tab, so the gap is major.
